paragraphs: We have spent more than a decade designing and testing a piloted, all-electric, vertical take-off and landing ("eVTOL") air taxi which we intend to operate in cities around the world. We intend to operate air taxi services both directly and through strategic partnerships, while also pursuing aircraft sales to distributors and expanding into defense and other specialized markets. Our mission is to help the world connect faster and more easily with the people and places that matter most by delivering a new form of clean, fast, quiet and convenient aerial transportation service. The Joby eVTOL is being designed to transport a pilot and up to four passengers - or a targeted payload of up to 1,000 pounds - at speeds of up to 200 mph. The aircraft is optimized for urban routes, with a target range of up to 100 miles on a single charge. According to our modeling, more than 99% of urban routes in cities such as New York City and Los Angeles are significantly shorter than this, enabling higher utilization through faster turnaround times of our aircraft. By combining the freedom of air travel with the efficiency of our aircraft, we expect to deliver journeys that are up to 10 times faster than driving, and it is our goal to steadily drive down end-user pricing in the years following commercial launch to make the service widely accessible.

Our aircraft has been specifically designed with multiple redundancies across systems and components for enhanced safety and to achieve a considerably lower noise footprint than that of similarly sized conventional aircraft or helicopters. It is quiet at takeoff and near silent when flying overhead, which we anticipate will allow us to operate from new vertiport locations nearer to where people live and work, in addition to utilizing the more than 5,000 heliport and airport infrastructure facilities already in existence in the U.S.

We are in the process of certifying our aircraft with the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA"). This involves a rigorous process of design, testing, verification and quality control. We have also begun working with regulators in other countries, including the United Kingdom, Japan, South Korea, Australia, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates ("UAE") to pursue commercialization opportunities in those markets. While foreign certification in many
countries leverages our work with the FAA, in some, such as the UAE, it may also provide a path to commercial operations prior to receiving certification in the United States.

We have identified three potential routes to market for our electric air taxi: (1) Joby owned and operated air taxi service (2) affiliate owned and operated service and (3) direct sales & defense. We plan to manufacture, operate and sell our aircraft, and are building a vertically integrated transportation company to maximize the value of our investments. In addition to building a novel aircraft, we are also building both an air taxi service and a next-generation aviation company. Elevate OS is our proprietary operating system that integrates data across aircraft build, operations and maintenance - establishing a scalable, software-enabled platform designed to improve efficiency and performance as our networks grow. At the front-end, we are developing a convenient consumer app to deliver the first on-demand, aerial ridesharing service. We are targeting carrying our first passengers in 2026. We believe this vertically-integrated business model will generate the greatest economic returns over time, while providing us with end-to-end control over the customer experience to optimize for customer safety, comfort and value. Vertical integration is also the key to fast design, test and launch iterations, as well as limiting our dependence on outside suppliers while developing valuable know-how and intellectual property in-house.

We operate a powertrain and electronics engineering and manufacturing facility in San Carlos, California, as well as 130,000 square feet of additive and subtractive manufacturing, machining, aircraft assembly and flight test facilities in Marina, California. With local support from California state incentives and grants, in 2025, we completed construction of a new 226,000 square foot building at our Marina site to support manufacturing and training. These facilities are utilized to design, build and test the components, systems and assemblies for our aircraft as we refine our design and hone our production processes. We believe that our California operations will both be able to support our initial low-rate production plans as well as serve as a testing and development facility for future innovations. Our high-rate production facility is planned for Dayton, Ohio where we purchased a 40,300 square foot facility in 2024 and an additional 728,000 square foot facility in January 2026 that has the potential to support significant growth over time. With strong financial incentives and support from state and local governments, we look forward to expanding our manufacturing in Ohio, the birthplace of aviation, as our business grows.

In August 2025, we acquired Blade Urban Air Mobility, Inc. and its subsidiaries ("Blade") which operates a technology-powered, global urban air mobility platform through which they provide air charter broker and other services. Following the acquisition, Blade continues to operate its air charter broker service as our wholly owned subsidiary. We expect the acquisition to provide immediate market access, including an established customer base, operational expertise, airport relationships and infrastructure across key urban corridors in New York City and Southern Europe. We expect our Blade operations to support our go-to-market strategy by providing near-term operating experience and customer insights, and by contributing relationships and infrastructure that we expect to leverage as we prepare for certification and the eventual launch of our eVTOL service.

Our preparations for commercial passenger service also includes forming sector-leading relationships with partners such as Toyota, Uber, and Delta Air Lines, each of whom have invested in Joby. We have also established relationships with global partners such as ANA Airlines in Japan, the Road and Transport Authority in Dubai and with Abdul Latif Jameel (ALJ) (a diversified Saudi-based business group), with whom we entered into a memorandum of understanding in June 2025 to explore opportunities to support distribution and operations in Saudi Arabia and the broader Middle East. We have also established relationships with infrastructure providers including fixed base operators and landing site partners such as Atlantic Aviation, Helo Holdings, Inc. ("HHI") and Skyports to facilitate infrastructure development in key markets. Additionally, we have long-standing relationships with U.S. federal government agencies.

Joby Aero, Inc. ("Legacy Joby") was incorporated in Delaware on November 21, 2016. In August 2021, Legacy Joby and Reinvent Technology Partners, a Cayman Islands exempted company and special purpose acquisition company ("RTP"), completed a merger and other transactions pursuant to which a subsidiary of RTP was merged with and into Legacy Joby and Legacy Joby survived as a wholly owned subsidiary of RTP. In connection with the transactions, RTP changed its name to Joby Aviation, Inc.

Our team of world-class engineers has been working for more than a decade to develop an aircraft specifically designed for aerial ridesharing. Over that period, we have built a team that is deeply committed to vertically integrated engineering, testing, prototyping and manufacturing. Developing much of the aircraft in-house has required greater up-front investment, but has also allowed us to develop systems and components that are specifically engineered for their intended applications. We believe this has resulted in an aircraft with best-in-class capabilities across key performance metrics, while reducing reliance on program critical third-party suppliers that add cost to the final product and risk to development and certification schedules.
We designed our aircraft to be safe, quiet and performant - all characteristics that we believe are critical to unlocking the urban aerial ridesharing market.

•Safe: Distributed electric propulsion has greater redundancy than centrally-located internal combustion engines. Each of our six propellers is powered by two independent electric motors, each in turn driven by independent drive-units. Each drive-unit draws power from one of four separate batteries onboard the aircraft.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
Certification & Regulatory
We may be unable to obtain relevant regulatory approvals for the commercialization of our aircraft or operation of our mobility service, either in the United States or in foreign markets.
Regulatory authorities may disagree with our view that integrating our service into the National Airspace System is possible without changes to existing regulations and procedures.
If current airspace regulations are not modified to increase air traffic capacity, our business could be subject to considerable capacity limitations.
Changes in government regulation could increase our operating costs or extend our certification timeline.
We may be subject to security regulation that will increase our operating costs.
Global trade policies, including tariffs, could adversely affect our operations.

We are subject to rapidly changing and increasingly restrictive laws, regulations and other obligations relating to privacy, data protection, and data security, which may be costly and difficult to comply with.
Market & Service
The market for UAM has not been established with precision. Customers may be reluctant to adopt this new form of mobility, or to pay our projected prices.
We may face delays in launching our commercial service.
Errors or vulnerabilities in software code could harm our business.
We may be unable to reduce end-user pricing at rates sufficient to drive growth for our service.
Our competitors may commercialize their technology before us, or we may not be able to fully capture the first mover advantage that we anticipate.
If we are unable to integrate our service with ground transportation services it may limit customer adoption and harm our business.
Customers may not differentiate our services from our competitors.
Our prospects may be adversely affected by changes in consumer preferences, discretionary spending and other economic conditions that affect demand for our services.

If we are unable to obtain and maintain adequate facilities and infrastructure, including access to key infrastructure such as airports, we may be unable to offer our service in a way that is useful to passengers.
Our aircraft utilization may be lower than expected due to weather and other factors.
Aircraft and Production
Our aircraft may fail to achieve performance expectations.
We may not be able to produce aircraft in the volumes and on the timelines we project.
Crashes, accidents or incidents of eVTOL and other aircraft could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
We will initially rely on a single type of aircraft to support our commercial UAM business, which makes us vulnerable to design defects or mechanical problems.
We depend on suppliers and service partners for raw materials, parts and components.
Our aircraft may require maintenance at frequencies or at costs which are unexpected.
U.S. Government Contracts and Pre-Certification Operations
The U.S. government may modify or terminate one or more of our existing contracts.
We may be unable to grow our relationship with the U.S. government and the Department of Defense.
We conduct a portion of our business pursuant to U.S. government contracts, which are subject to unique risks.
Risks Related to our Blade Air Charter Operations
We may not realize the anticipated benefits of our acquisition of Blade, and the acquisition may expose us to integration challenges, additional liabilities and costs, and potential dilution.

We could suffer losses and adverse publicity stemming from accidents involving small aircraft, helicopters, or charter flights generally and, in particular, from any accident or incident involving Blade charter flights.
The markets for our Blade offerings are still in relatively early stages of growth, and such markets may not continue to grow, or may grow more slowly than we expect.
If we are unable to obtain and maintain adequate facilities and infrastructure, we may be unable to offer our existing Blade flight schedule and to expand our route network in the future.
We rely on our third-party operators to provide and operate aircraft. If such third-party operators do not perform adequately or terminate their relationships with us, our costs may increase.
Risks Related to Our Finances and Operations
We have incurred significant losses since inception, we expect to incur losses in the future, and we may not be able to achieve or maintain profitability.
We will need additional capital in the future, including to build high-volume manufacturing, and to develop a vertiport network to support a high-volume service.
We have broad discretion in how we use our assets, and we may not use them effectively.
Our ability to use our net operating loss carryforwards and certain other tax attributes may be limited.

The commercialization of new aircraft and the operation of an aerial mobility service requires certain regulatory authorizations and certifications, including Type Certification, Production Certification and an air carrier certificate issued by the FAA under Part 119 with Part 135 operations specifications. While we have received our Part 135 Air Carrier Certificate and anticipate being able to obtain the remaining required authorizations and certifications, we may be unable to do so on the timeline we project or at all. Circumstances outside of our control could delay the receipt of our required certifications. For example, FAA staffing depends, in large part, on the annual appropriations process and the agency's ability to retain and recruit sufficient resources with relevant experience and expertise. Failure to pass an annual appropriation bill has in the past resulted in temporary government shutdowns. A future shutdown, or a failure by Congress to pass an FAA reauthorization bill (or extension) could delay the rulemaking and certification process. Additionally, recent focus on reducing the size of the federal workforce could negatively impact the availability of resources within the FAA which could delay our progress towards certification.

We are also pursuing certification of our aircraft and approval to operate our services in other countries. While many of these countries have established processes for validating a type certificate issued by the FAA, others, such as the UAE, are developing new processes to leverage our work with the FAA and provide a path for approval of initial operations that could precede type certification in the United States. The regulatory agencies charged with granting approval for our aircraft and our services in other countries may be subject to many of the same funding and staffing risks that exist in the United States. Additionally, pursuing certification and operations outside the United States is subject to additional risks, including regulatory regimes that may be less familiar to us or may have less experience in certifying and approving new and novel aircraft. If we fail to obtain any of the required authorizations or certificates, or do so in a timely manner, or any of these authorizations or certificates are modified, suspended or revoked after we obtain them, we may be unable to launch our commercial service or do so on the timelines we project and may have an adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

There are a number of existing laws, regulations and standards that apply to our aircraft and our service, including standards that were not originally intended to apply to eVTOL aircraft or air taxi services. While our aircraft and our service are designed, at launch, to operate within the existing U.S. regulatory framework, the FAA or other regulatory authorities within the markets in which we intend to operate may disagree with this view, which may prohibit, restrict, or delay our ability to launch in the relevant market. In addition, any changes to the NAS, as a result of privatization or otherwise, could increase the costs to operate our service. Finally, regulatory authorities have in the past and may in the future introduce changes specifically to address high-volume flights that could delay our ability to launch our service and have an adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

A failure to increase air traffic capacity in the airspace serving key markets, including around major airports, could create capacity limitations for our future operations and could have a material adverse effect on our business. Weaknesses in the NAS and the Air Traffic Control ("ATC") system, such as outdated procedures and technologies, could result in capacity constraints during peak travel periods or adverse weather conditions, resulting in delays and disruptions to our service. While our aircraft is designed to operate in the NAS under existing rules, our business at scale will likely require airspace allocation for UAM operations and could result in regulatory changes. Our inability to obtain sufficient access to the NAS or to comply with any regulatory changes could increase our costs and pricing of our services, which could reduce demand and have an adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Aerospace manufacturers and aircraft operators are subject to extensive regulatory and legal requirements that involve significant compliance costs. In May 2022, the FAA decided to certify eVTOLs under the "powered lift" classification, rather than existing Part 23 requirements for Normal Category Airplanes. The FAA finalized the relevant operational regulations, or Special Federal Aviation Regulations ("SFARs"), for eVTOL aircraft in October 2024. If the FAA requires further modification to our existing G-1 certification basis, or if there are other regulatory changes or revisions to the SFARs or other regulations, this could delay our ability to obtain type certification, and could delay our ability to launch our commercial passenger service.

We have spent more than a decade designing and testing a piloted all-electric, vertical take-off and landing ("eVTOL") air taxi that we intend to operate as part of a fast, quiet and convenient service in cities around the world. The aircraft is quiet when taking off, near silent when flying overhead and is being designed to transport a pilot and up to four passengers - or a targeted payload of up to 1,000 pounds - at speeds of up to 200 mph. The low noise enabled by the all-electric powertrain will allow the aircraft to operate around dense, urban areas while blending into the background noise of cities. In August 2025, we added another milestone flight to thousands of successful test flights, with our piloted eVTOL flight between two public airports in FAA-controlled airspace, demonstrating operational maturity and integration with existing air traffic. As the first eVTOL aircraft developer to receive a signed, stage 4 G-1 certification basis which was subsequently published in final form in the Federal Register, we believe we are well positioned to be the first eVTOL manufacturer to earn standard airworthiness certification from the Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA"). We have multiple special airworthiness certificates already issued by the FAA for our fleet of pre-type certification aircraft.

We have identified three potential routes to market: (1) Joby owned and operated air taxi service (2) affiliate owned and operated service and (3) direct sales and defense. We plan to manufacture, operate and sell our aircraft, and are building a vertically integrated transportation company to maximize the value of our investments. In addition to building a novel aircraft, we are also building a proprietary operating system that integrates data across aircraft build, operations and maintenance. At the front end, we are developing a convenient app to deliver the first on-demand, aerial ridesharing service. We are targeting carrying our first passengers in 2026. We believe this vertically-integrated business model will generate the greatest economic returns over time, while providing us with end-to-end control and information regarding customer experience to optimize for customer safety, comfort and value.

In August 2025, we acquired Blade Urban Air Mobility, Inc. and its subsidiaries ("Blade"), a technology-powered, global urban air mobility platform. Following the acquisition, Blade continues to operate its air charter broker service as our wholly owned subsidiary. The transaction is expected to unlock immediate market access, including an established customer base, operational expertise, airport relationships and infrastructure across key urban corridors in New York City and Southern Europe and allow us to combine our best-in-class technology with Blade's experience in delivering premium customer transportation at scale.

Since our inception in 2009, we have been primarily engaged in research and development of eVTOL aircraft. We have incurred net operating losses and negative cash flows from operations in every year since our inception. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $2,785.6 million. We have funded our operations primarily with proceeds from the issuance of stock, convertible notes and the proceeds from our merger in August 2021 with Reinvent Technology Partners ("RTP"), a special purpose acquisition company, through which we became a publicly-traded company.
See the section entitled "Risk Factors" for a further discussion of these considerations.

Our revenue will be directly tied to the continued development of short distance aerial transportation. While we believe the global market for UAM will be large, it remains undeveloped and there is no guarantee of future demand. We delivered our first aircraft for initial service operations with the DOD in September 2023 and are targeting carrying our first passengers in 2026. Our business will require significant investment leading up to launching these services, including, but not limited to, final engineering designs, prototyping and testing, manufacturing, software development, certification, pilot training, infrastructure and commercialization.

We believe one of the primary drivers for adoption of our aerial ridesharing service is the value proposition and time savings offered by aerial mobility relative to traditional ground-based transportation. Additional factors impacting the pace of adoption of our aerial ridesharing service may include but are not limited to: perceptions about eVTOL quality, safety, performance and cost; perceptions about the limited range over which eVTOL may be flown on a single battery charge; volatility in the cost of oil and gasoline; availability of competing forms of transportation, such as ground, air taxi or ride-hailing services; the development of adequate infrastructure; consumers' perception about the safety, convenience and cost of transportation using eVTOL relative to ground-based alternatives; and increases in fuel efficiency, autonomy, or electrification of cars. In addition, macroeconomic factors could impact demand for UAM services, particularly if end-user pricing is at a premium to ground-based transportation alternatives. We anticipate initial operations in the U.S. under the eIPP to be followed by operations in selected high-density metropolitan areas where traffic congestion is particularly acute and operating conditions are suitable for early eVTOL operations.

We believe that the primary sources of competition for our service are ground-based mobility solutions, other eVTOL developers/operators and local/regional incumbent aircraft charter services. While we expect to be first to market with an eVTOL facilitated aerial ridesharing service, we expect this industry to be dynamic and increasingly competitive; and our competitors could get to market before us, either generally or in specific markets. Even if we are first to market, we may not receive any competitive advantage or may be overtaken by other competitors. If new or existing companies launch competing solutions in the markets in which we intend to operate or obtain large-scale capital investment, we may face increased competition. Additionally, our competitors may benefit from our efforts in developing consumer and community acceptance for eVTOL aircraft and aerial ridesharing, making it easier for them to obtain the permits and authorizations required to operate an aerial ridesharing service in the markets in which we intend to launch or in other markets. If we do not capture the first mover advantage that we anticipate, it may harm our business, financial condition, operating results and prospects.

We signed a revised, stage 4 "G-1" certification basis for our aircraft with the FAA in July 2022, which was published in final form in the Federal Register in March 2024. This agreement lays out the specific requirements that need to be met by our aircraft for it to be certified for commercial operations. Reaching this milestone marks a key step towards certifying any new aircraft in the U.S. We think of the FAA type certification process in five stages and have made significant progress towards certification. We have completed or substantially completed three of these five stages and are more than halfway through the fourth stage.

In 2022, we received our Part 135 operating certificate, which is required for us to operate an on-demand air service and allows us to operate the service with conventional aircraft. In October 2024, the FAA published the Special Federal Aviation Regulations ("SFARs"), which include operational regulations related to eVTOLs. We will need to comply with these SFARs as we add our aircraft to our Part 135 operating certificate. If the FAA requires further modifications to our existing G-1 certification basis, makes subsequent modifications to the SFARs, or if there are other regulatory changes or revisions, this could delay our ability to obtain type certification, and could delay our ability to launch our commercial passenger service.

We expect the FAA type certificate will be validated in certain international markets pursuant to bilateral agreements between the FAA and its counterpart civil aviation authorities in other countries. In 2022, we applied for aircraft certification in the United Kingdom and Japan. In 2023, we signed an agreement with Road and Transport Authority of Dubai ("RTA") for Joby to provide air taxi services in Dubai. The RTA agreement includes a roadmap for local approval by the UAE General Civil Aviation Authority that could precede type certification by the FAA. These arrangements provide a means of efficient international expansion as we develop commercial operations around the world.

In addition to certifying our aircraft, we will also need to obtain authorizations and certifications related to the production of our aircraft and the deployment of our aerial ridesharing service. We anticipate being able to meet the requirements of such authorizations and certifications. If we fail to obtain any of the required authorizations or certifications, or do so in a timely manner, or if any of these authorizations or certifications are modified, suspended or revoked after we obtain them, we may be unable to launch our commercial service or do so on the timelines we project, which would have adverse effects on our business, prospects, financial condition and/or results of operations.

In December 2020, we became, to our knowledge, the first company to receive airworthiness approval for an eVTOL aircraft for a flight clearance from the USAF to conduct a government test. Our multi-year relationship with the DOD and other U.S. government agencies has provided us with a compelling opportunity to more thoroughly understand the operational capabilities and maintenance profiles of our aircraft in advance of commercial launch.

paragraphs: 本公司已投入超過十年的時間設計並測試一架有人駕駛、全電動、垂直起降（"eVTOL"）空中計程車，並計畫在世界各地的城市運營。本公司計畫透過直接運營及戰略合作夥伴的方式提供空中計程車服務，同時也計畫透過經銷商銷售飛機，並拓展至防禦及其他專業市場。本公司使命為透過提供一種全新形式的潔淨、快速、安靜且便利的空中運輸服務，協助世界更快更輕鬆地連接最重要的人員與地點。Joby eVTOL 設計用以運載駕駛員及最多四名乘客，或最多 1,000 磅的貨物，速度可達每小時 200 英里。此飛機針對城區路線進行優化，單次充電的目標航程可達 100 英里。根據我們的模型顯示，在紐約市與洛杉磯等城市中，超過 99% 的城區路線明顯短於此，使我們的飛機能透過更快的轉場時間提高使用率。透過結合空中旅行的自由與本公司飛機的效率，我們預期能提供比駕駛快達十倍的旅程，並計畫在商業啟動後的幾年內逐步降低終端用戶價格，使服務更廣泛可及。
本公司飛機特別設計有多重系統與零組件的備用設計，以提升安全性，並達到遠低於同尺寸傳統飛機或直升機的噪音足跡。此飛機在起飛時安靜，飛行時幾乎無聲，我們預期這將使我們能運營位於居民與工作地點附近的新型垂直起降機場，同時也能利用美國現有的超過 5,000 個直升機場與機場基礎設施。
本公司正在進行與美國聯邦航空管理局（"FAA"）的飛機認證程序。此程序包含嚴謹的設計、測試、驗證與品質控制過程。本公司也已開始與其他國家的監管機構合作，包括英國、日本、韓國、澳洲、沙特阿拉伯王國與阿拉伯聯合大公國（"UAE"），以追求這些市場的商業化機會。雖然許多國家的外國認證程序會利用我們與 FAA 的工作，但在某些國家，例如 UAE，也可能提供在獲得美國認證前進行商業運營的途徑。
在這些國家，外國認證程序會利用我們與 FAA 的工作，但在某些國家，例如 UAE，也可能提供在獲得美國認證前進行商業運營的途徑。

我們已識別出三個潛在的市場通路，用以銷售我們的電動空中計程車：(1) Joby 自營自營的空中計程車服務 (2) 關係企業自營自營的服務以及 (3) 直接銷售與防禦。我們計畫製造、營運並銷售我們的飛機，並建立一個垂直整合的運輸公司，以最大化我們投資的價值。除了建立一款新型飛機，我們同時也在建立空中計程車服務與下一代航空公司。Elevate OS 是我們的專屬作業系統，整合飛機製造、營運與維護的資料 - 建立一個可擴展、軟體驅動的平台，設計用以隨著我們的網路成長，提高效率與表現。在前端，我們正在開發一個便利的消費者應用程式，提供首個即時、空中計程車服務。我們預計在 2026 年開始載運首批乘客。我們相信這種垂直整合的商業模式，將在長遠時間內產生最大的經濟回報，同時也讓我們對客戶體驗擁有端到端的控制，以優化客戶的安全、舒適與價值。垂直整合也是快速設計、測試與發佈迭代的關鍵，同時也能減少對外部供應商的依賴，同時在內部發展寶貴的知識與智慧財產權。

我們在加州聖卡拉路斯經營一個動力系統與電子工程與製造設施，同時也在馬裏納市擁有 13 萬平方英尺的增材與減材製造、機械加工、飛機組裝與飛行測試設施。在加州州政府的當地支持下，包括州政府的激勵措施與補助金，我們在 2025 年完成了馬裏納市新興 226,000 平方英尺建築物的建設，以支持製造與訓練。這些設施用於設計、製造與測試我們飛機的零組件、系統與組裝，隨著我們精進設計與優化製造流程。我們相信，我們在加州的運營將能支持我們初始的低速率生產計畫，同時也能作為未來創新測試與開發的設施。我們的高速率生產設施預計在俄亥俄州代頓市，我們在 2024 年購入了一座 40,300 平方英尺的設施，並在 2026 年 1 月購入了另外一處 728,000 平方英尺的設施，該設施有潛力在長遠時間內支持顯著的成長。在州與地方政府強大的財政激勵措施與支持下，我們期待隨著業務成長，擴展我們在俄亥俄州的製造業務，俄亥俄州是航空的發源地。

2025 年 8 月，我們收購了 Blade Urban Air Mobility, Inc. 及其子公司（"Blade"），該公司透過科技驅動的全球都市空中移動平台，提供空中包機經紀及其他服務。收購後，Blade 繼續以其空中包機經紀服務運作，作為我們的 wholly owned subsidiary。我們預期此收購將提供即時的市場准入，包括已建立的客戶羣、運營專業知識、機場關係與基礎設施，遍及紐約市與南歐的關鍵都市走廊。我們預期 Blade 的運營將支持我們的市場進入策略，透過提供短期運營經驗與客戶見解，並透過貢獻關係與基礎設施，我們預期將在準備認證與最終發佈 eVTOL 服務時加以利用。

我們為商業乘客服務所做的準備，也包括與如 Toyota、Uber 與 Delta Air Lines 等行業領先者建立關係，這些公司均投資於 Joby。我們也與全球夥伴如日本的 ANA 航空公司、杜拜的交通與運輸管理局，以及沙特阿拉伯的 Abdul Latif Jameel（ALJ）（一家多元化沙特阿拉伯企業集團）建立關係，我們在 2025 年 6 月與 ALJ 籤訂備忘錄，探討支持沙特阿拉伯與更廣泛中東地區分銷與運營的機會。我們也與基礎設施供應商建立關係，包括固定基地運營商與降落場夥伴，如 Atlantic Aviation、Helo Holdings, Inc.（"HHI"）與 Skyports，以促進關鍵市場的基礎設施發展。此外，我們也與美國聯邦政府機構有長期關係。

Joby Aero, Inc. ("Legacy Joby") 於 2016 年 11 月 21 日在特拉華州成立。2021 年 8 月，Legacy Joby 與 Reinvent Technology Partners，一家開曼羣島豁免公司及特殊目的收購公司 ("RTP") 完成合併及其他交易，根據該交易，RTP 的子公司與 Legacy Joby 合併，且 Legacy Job, Inc. 繼續作為 RTP 的 wholly owned subsidiary。根據交易，RTP 改名為 Joby Aviation, Inc.

我們的總部位於加州聖克魯斯市 333 Encinal 街，郵遞區號 95060。電話號碼為 (831) 201-6700。我們的網站網址為 www.jobyaviation.com。美國證券交易委員會 ("SEC") 保有網站 www.sec.gov，該網站包含上市公司電子檔提交的報告、股東權利說明書與資訊聲明及其他資訊。我們亦於網站 ir.jobyaviation.com 提供所有向 SEC 提交或提供之 SEC 檔案，於合理期間內免費提供。我們有適用於執行長、董事與員工的道德準則，包括執行長、財務長、會計長或執行類似職務之人員。該道德準則於網站 ir.jobyaviation.com 可取得。我們有意於網站上公開任何法律上要求的關於道德準則修正或豁免的資訊，而非透過提交
Current Report on Form 8-K。本年度報告中提及的任何網站資訊並非本報告或任何其他提交或提供給 SEC 的報告的一部分或參考資料。

我們的全球級工程團隊已投入超過十年的時間，專注於開發專為空中 ridesharing 設計的飛機。在這段期間，我們已組建一支深具承諾的團隊，專注於垂直整合的工程、測試、原型製作與製造。許多飛機的開發在內部進行，這需要更高的前期投資，但也使我們能開發出專為其預期用途設計的系統與零組件。我們相信這已使我們的飛機在關鍵性能指標上具備業界最佳的表現，同時降低對關鍵第三方供應商的依賴，這些供應商會增加最終產品的成本與開發與認證時程的風險。
我們設計飛機時，著重於安全性、靜音與性能 - 我們相信這些特點對開發城市空中 ridesharing 市場至關重要。
•安全：分散式電動推進系統具有比集中式內燃機更高的冗餘性。我們的六個螺旋槳每個均由兩個獨立電動機驅動，每個電動機又由獨立的驅動單元驅動。每個驅動單元從飛機上的四個獨立電池中獲取電力。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析提供資訊，本公司管理階層認為與評估及瞭解我們合併後之營運成果與財務狀況有關。討論應與我們合併財務報表及相關附註一同閱讀，這些內容出現在本年度報告的其他地方。我們已選擇省略對合併財務報表所涵蓋之最早三個會計年度的討論。請參閱我們於2025年2月27日提交的2024年12月31日結年度10-K年度報告中，位於「管理階層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」項目（Item 7）的內容，以參考對2023年12月31日結年度財務年度的討論，這是三個財務年度中最早的一個。本討論與分析包含前瞻性聲明，這些聲明涉及風險與不確定性。請參閱本年度報告中標題為「關於前瞻性聲明之特別說明」的章節。

我們已投入超過十年的時間設計與測試一架無人駕駛電動垂直起降（"eVTOL"）空中計程車，我們預計將此機種作為一種快速、安靜且便利的服務，用於全球各城市的運輸。此飛機在起飛時相當安靜，在飛行時幾乎無聲，並設計為可運載一名駕駛員與最多四名乘客，或最多1,000磅的貨物，速度可達每小時200英里。此飛機針對城市路線進行優化，單次充電的飛行距離目標為最多100英里。根據我們的模型顯示，在紐約市與洛杉磯等城市的大多數城市路線，超過99%的路線都明顯短於此，這將使我們的飛機能有更高的使用率，因較短的轉場時間。透過結合空中旅行的自由與我們飛機的效率，我們預期能提供比駕駛快達十倍的旅程，並希望在商業啟動後的幾年內逐步降低終端用戶的價格，使此服務更易於取得。電動動力系統所帶來的低噪音，將使飛機能在密集的城市地區運作，並融入城市的背景噪音中。2025年8月，我們又增加了另一個里程碑飛行，與數千次成功的測試飛行一樣，我們進行了兩座公共機場之間的駕駛員駕駛eVTOL飛行，這是在聯邦航空管理局（"FAA"）管制空域中進行，顯示我們的運作成熟度與與現有空中交通的整合。作為第一家獲得簽署、第四階段G-1認證基礎的eVTOL飛機開發商，此後該認證基礎已正式發表於聯邦註冊處，我們相信我們已處於優勢，成為第一家獲得聯邦航空管理局（"FAA"）標準適航認證的eVTOL製造商。我們已獲得多項特殊適航認證，這些認證是由聯邦航空管理局（"FAA"）為我們的預型認證飛機隊發出的。

我們已識別出三個潛在的市場進入途徑：(1) Joby擁有並運營的空中計程車服務 (2) 關係企業擁有並運營的服務 (3) 直接銷售與防禦。我們計畫製造、運營並銷售我們的飛機，並正在建立一個垂直整合的運輸公司，以最大化我們投資的價值。除了建造一項新型飛機，我們也在建造一個專屬的作業系統，整合飛機建造、運營與維護的數據。在前端，我們正在開發一個方便的應用程式，以提供首個即時需求的空中計程車服務。我們預計在2026年開始運載首批乘客。我們相信這種垂直整合的商業模式將在長遠內產生最大的經濟回報，同時也讓我們擁有對客戶體驗的端到端控制與資訊，以優化客戶的安全、舒適與價值。

2025年8月，我們收購了Blade Urban Air Mobility, Inc.及其子公司（"Blade"），一家以科技為動力的全球都市空中運輸平台。在收購後，Blade繼續運營其空中包機經紀服務，作為我們的 wholly owned subsidiary。此交易預期將立即打開市場准入，包括已建立的客戶羣、運營專業知識、機場關係與基礎設施，遍及紐約市與南歐等關鍵都市走廊，並讓我們能將我們的領先科技與Blade在大規模提供高品質客戶運輸方面的經驗結合。
自2009年成立以來，我們主要從事eVTOL飛機的研究與開發。自成立以來，我們每年都出現淨營運虧損與營運現金流為負。截至2025年12月31日，我們累積虧損為2785.6百萬美元。我們主要透過發行股票、可轉換票據以及2021年8月與Reinvent Technology Partners（"RTP"）合併的資金，來資助我們的運營，RTP是一家特殊目的收購公司，透過此合併我們成為一家上市公司。
請參閱「風險因素」部分，以進一步討論這些考量。
我們的收入將直接與短距離空中運輸的持續發展相關。雖然我們相信全球UAM市場將非常龐大，但該市場目前尚未開發，未來需求並無保證。我們在2023年9月交付了首架飛機，用於美國國防部的初始服務運作，並預計在2026年開始運載首批乘客。我們的業務將需要大量的投資，以啟動這些服務，包括但不限於最終工程設計、原型製作與測試、製造、軟體開發、認證、駕駛員培訓、基礎設施與商業化。

我們認為，我們空中計程車服務的採用率之一個主要驅動因素是空中運輸相對於傳統地面運輸所帶來的價值與時間節省。影響我們空中計程車服務採用速度的其他因素可能包括但不限於：對eVTOL品質、安全性、性能與成本的觀感；對eVTOL在單次電池充電下飛行範圍有限的觀感；石油與汽油成本的波動；競爭性運輸方式的可得性，例如地面運輸、空中計程車或叫車服務；基礎設施的發展；消費者對使用eVTOL進行運輸的安全性、便利性與成本的觀感，相對於地面運輸的替代方案；以及汽車燃油效率、自動化或電動化的提升。此外，總體經濟因素可能影響UAM服務的需求，特別是在終端用戶價格高於地面運輸替代方案的情況下。我們預期美國將首先在eIPP下進行初始運作，隨後在交通壅塞特別嚴重且運作條件適合早期eVTOL運作的選定高密度都會區進行運作。

我們認為，我們服務的主要競爭來源為地面移動解決方案、其他 eVTOL 開發者/營運者以及當地/區域性現有航空包機服務。雖然我們預期會率先在市場推出 eVTOL 促進的空中共乘服務，但我們預期這個產業將是動態且越來越競爭；我們的競爭對手可能在我們之前進駐市場，無論是整體或特定市場。即使我們是市場先發者，我們可能不會獲得任何競爭優勢，或可能被其他競爭對手超越。如果新興或現有公司推出競爭解決方案在我們預期營運的市場，或取得大規模資本投資，我們可能面臨增加的競爭。此外，我們的競爭對手可能受益於我們在開發消費者與社區對 eVTOL 飛機與空中共乘服務的接受度方面的努力，使他們更容易取得在我們預期發佈或其它市場營運空中共乘服務所需的許可與授權。如果我們未能把握預期的先發優勢，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與前景造成傷害。
我們在 2022 年 7 月與 FAA 簽訂了修正後的第 4 階段 "G-1" 認證基礎，該協議於 2024 年 3 月在聯邦登記處以最終形式發表。此協議說明了我們飛機必須達到的特定要求，以獲得商業營運的認證。達成這個里程碑標誌著美國認證任何新飛機的重要步驟。我們將 FAA 類型認證程序視為五個階段，並已取得重大進展。我們已完成或幾乎完成這五個階段中的三個，且已超過第四階段的一半。

2022 年，我們獲得了 Part 135 運營證書，這是我們運營按需航空服務所必需的，並允許我們使用傳統飛機運營該服務。2024 年 10 月，FAA 發布了特殊聯邦航空規則（"SFARs"），其中包括與 eVTOL 相關的運營規則。我們在將飛機加入 Part 135 運營證書時，將需要遵守這些 SFARs。如果 FAA 要求進一步修改我們現有的 G-1 認證基礎，或對 SFARs 進行後續修改，或有其他法規變更或修訂，這可能會延遲我們獲得類型認證的能力，並可能延遲我們推出商業乘客服務的能力。

我們預期 FAA 類型證書將根據 FAA 與其他國家民航當局之間的雙邊協議，在某些國際市場進行驗證。2022 年，我們申請了英國與日本的飛機認證。2023 年，我們與迪拜道路與運輸當局（"RTA"）簽訂協議，由 Joby 在迪拜提供空中計程車服務。RTA 協議包含一個由阿聯酋民航當局進行本地批准的路線圖，這可能在 FAA 類型認證之前進行。這些安排為我們在全球發展商業運營提供了一種高效的國際擴張方式。
除了認證我們的飛機，我們還需要取得與我們飛機生產及空中共乘服務部署相關的許可與認證。我們預期能夠符合這些許可與認證的要求。如果我們未能取得任何所需的許可或認證，或未能在預期時間內取得，或這些許可或認證在取得後被修改、中止或撤銷，我們可能無法推出商業服務，或無法在預期時間內推出，這將對我們的業務、前景、財務狀況與/或營運結果產生不利影響。
2020 年 12 月，我們成為，據我們所知，首家獲得 eVTOL 飛機適航批准的公司，以取得美國空軍（USAF）的飛行許可，用於進行政府測試。我們與美國國防部（DOD）及其他美國政府機構的多年合作關係，為我們提供了深入瞭解我們飛機運營能力與維護特徵的機會，這是在商業發佈前的關鍵階段。

headings: 與本公司及產業相關之風險
認證與法規
本公司可能無法取得美國或外國市場商業化飛機或運營移動服務所需之相關法規核准。
法規主管機關可能不同意本公司認為將本服務整合至國家空域系統中無需修改現有法規及程序之觀點。
若現行空域法規未修改以增加空域交通容量，本公司業務可能面臨相當程度之容量限制。
政府法規之變更可能增加本公司營運成本或延長本公司認證時程。
本公司可能面臨安全法規之管制，進而增加營運成本。
全球貿易政策，包括關稅，可能對本公司營運造成不利影響。
本公司受制於快速變動且日益嚴格的法律、法規及其他義務，涉及隱私權、資料保護及資料安全，這些義務可能導致成本高昂且難以符合要求。
市場與服務
UAM 市場尚未明確建立。客戶可能對採用此種新型移動方式或支付我們預期的價格持保留態度。
本公司可能面臨延遲推出商業服務的風險。
軟體程式碼中的錯誤或漏洞可能對本公司業務造成損害。
本公司可能無法以足夠的速率降低終端用戶價格，以推動服務成長。
競爭對手可能在本公司之前商業化其技術，或本公司可能無法完全把握預期的先發優勢。
若本公司無法將服務與地面運輸服務整合，可能限制客戶採用，並對本公司業務造成損害。
客戶可能無法將我們的服務與競爭對手區分開來。
我們的前景可能因消費者偏好、可支配支出及其他影響我們服務需求的經濟條件而受到不利影響。
若我們無法取得並維持足夠的設施與基礎建設，包括對關鍵基礎建設如機場的存取，我們可能無法以對乘客有用的方 式提供服務。
由於天氣及其他因素，我們的飛機使用率可能低於預期。
飛機與生產
我們的飛機可能無法達到預期的性能表現。
我們可能無法按預期的數量與時間表生產飛機。
eVTOL 及其他飛機的墜機、事故或事件可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
我們將 initially rely on 一種類型的飛機來支持我們的商業 UAM 業務，這使我們容易受到設計缺陷或機械問題的影響。
我們依賴供應商及服務夥伴提供原材料、零件及零組件。
我們的飛機可能需要以預期之外的頻率或成本進行維護。
美國政府契約及預認證作業
美國政府可能修改或終止我們現有的部分契約。
我們可能無法擴大與美國政府及國防部的關係。
我們部分業務係依據美國政府契約進行，這些契約面臨獨特的風險。
與我們 Blade Air 航空包機業務相關的風險
我們可能無法實現對 Blade 收購所預期的效益，且該收購可能使我們面臨整合挑戰、額外的負債與成本，以及潛在的股本稀釋。
我們可能因小型飛機、直升機或包機飛行的事故而遭受損失與負面宣傳，特別是任何涉及 Blade 包機飛行的事故或事件。
我們 Blade 產品的市場仍處於相對早期的成長階段，這些市場可能無法持續成長，或成長速度可能慢於我們預期。
若我們無法取得並維持足夠的設施與基礎建設，我們可能無法提供現有的 Blade 飛行排程，並在未來擴展航線網路。
我們依賴第三方營運商提供並營運飛機。若這些第三方營運商表現不佳或終止與我們的關係，我們的成本可能增加。
與我們財務與營運相關的風險
我們自成立以來已產生重大虧損，我們預期未來仍將產生虧損，且可能無法實現或維持盈利。
我們未來將需要額外資金，包括用於建立高產能製造，以及發展垂直起降機場網路以支持高產能服務。
本公司對於如何運用資產具有廣泛的裁量權，且可能無法有效運用。
本公司運用淨營業虧損結轉及某些其他稅務屬性之能力可能受到限制。
paragraphs: 在進行營運業務的過程中，我們面臨多種風險。我們所描述的任何風險因素都已影響或可能重大不利影響我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與品牌。若其中一個或數個風險與不確定性發生，本公司普通股的市場價格可能下跌，甚至大幅或永久下跌。"風險因素"中某些陳述為預測性陳述。請參閱"預測性陳述特別說明"。

新飛機的商業化與空中移動服務的營運需要某些法規授權與認證，包括型別認證、生產認證與由 FAA 根據第 119 章與第 135 章營運規範所頒發的航空運輸業者證書。雖然我們已取得第 135 章航空運輸業者證書，並預期能取得其餘所需授權與認證，但我們可能無法在預期時間表內或完全取得。我們無法控制的情況可能延宕我們取得所需認證。例如，FAA 的員工數量在很大程度上取決於年度預算程序與該機構保留並招募具有相關經驗與專業知識的資源能力。過去未能通過年度預演算法案導致暫時性政府停擺。未來停擺，或國會未能通過 FAA 再授權法案（或延長）可能延宕規則制定與認證程序。此外，近期對縮減聯邦僱員人數的關注可能對 FAA 內部資源的可用性產生負面影響，進而延宕我們取得認證的進度。

我們同時也在追求我們飛機的認證與在其他國家營運服務的批准。雖然許多國家已建立驗證由 FAA 頒發型別認證的程序，但其他國家，例如阿拉伯聯合大公國（UAE），正在發展新程序以利用我們與 FAA 的合作，並提供一條通往初始營運批准的路徑，這可能在美國的型別認證之前。在其他國家授予我們飛機與服務批准的法規機構可能面臨與美國相同的資金與人力風險。此外，追求在美國以外的認證與營運還涉及額外風險，包括可能對我們而言較不熟悉或經驗較少在認證與批准新型號飛機的法規體系。若我們未能取得任何所需授權或證書，或未能在預期時間內取得，或這些授權或證書在取得後被修改、暫停或吊銷，我們可能無法啟動商業服務，或無法在預期時間表內啟動，並可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運結果產生負面影響。

目前有許多現行法律、法規與標準適用於我們的飛機與服務，包括原本並未預期適用於 eVTOL 飛機或空中計程車服務的標準。雖然我們的飛機與服務在啟動時設計為在現行美國法規框架內運作，但 FAA 或其他在我們預期營運市場內的法規機構可能不同意此觀點，這可能禁止、限制或延宕我們在相關市場啟動的能力建立。此外，任何因私有化或其他原因導致 NAS 的變更，可能會增加我們服務的運營成本。最後，法規機構過去曾並可能未來引入針對高頻率航班的特定變更，這可能會延宕我們啟動服務的能力，並對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運結果產生負面影響。

若無法增加服務於關鍵市場（包括主要機場周圍）空域的空中交通容量，可能會對我們未來的運營造成容量限制，並對我們的業務產生重大負面影響。NAS 與空中交通管制（"ATC"）系統的弱點，例如過時的程序與技術，可能在高峯旅行時期或惡劣天氣條件下導致容量限制，進而造成服務延誤與中斷。雖然我們的飛機設計為在現行 NAS 規則下運作，但我們在規模營運時可能需要為 UAM 運作分配空域，這可能導致法規變更。我們無法取得足夠的 NAS 使用權或遵守任何法規變更，可能會增加我們服務的成本與價格，這可能會降低需求，並對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運結果產生負面影響。

航空航天製造商與飛機營運商需遵守廣泛的法規與法律要求，這涉及顯著的合規成本。2022 年 5 月，FAA 決定以 "動力升力" 分類認證 eVTOL 飛機，而非現行的 Part 23 要求的正常類別飛機。FAA 於 2024 年 10 月完成 eVTOL 飛機的相關運營規則，或稱為特殊聯邦航空規則（"SFARs"）。若 FAA 要求進一步修改我們現有的 G-1 認證基礎，或有其他法規變更或 SFARs 或其他規則的修訂，這可能會延宕我們取得型別認證的能力建立，並延宕我們啟動商業乘客服務的能力建立。
